label: CJEU C-40/17 — Fashion ID (joint controllership of plugins)
body: 2. A website operator embedding a social plugin (Facebook 'Like' button) causing the visitor's browser to transmit personal data to the plugin provider is a joint controller with the provider — but only for the collection and disclosure-by-transmission operations it actually co-determines. Not for subsequent operations carried out by the provider alone.
3. For Art. 6(1)(f) to apply, each of the joint controllers must independently pursue a legitimate interest.
4. The operator must obtain consent and provide Art. 13/14 transparency only as regards the operations it controls.

Why it matters: Reframed pixel/SDK embeddings as joint-controllership for the collection/transmission stage. Combined with C-210/16 Wirtschaftsakademie (page admin) and C-25/17 Jehovan todistajat — sets a broad joint-controllership doctrine.

UK status: Decided pre-Brexit-transition-end (2019), so assimilated (retained) EU case law in the UK — but UK higher courts may depart from it under the Retained EU Law (Revocation and Reform) Act 2023.
